scope: Talvora Memory Phase 2B: additive live-schema migration adds retention_class and claim_key, project identifiers are normalized, retention classes derive automatic expiry, and higher-authority evidence can supersede lower-authority stale claims while preserving audit history.

libraries.verified: Current SQLite guidance supports PRAGMA table_info for schema inspection, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN for additive migration, transactional bulk updates, indexes over new nullable columns, and FTS5 external-content synchronization triggers. Talvora Memory Phase 2B uses runtime schema inspection before adding retention_class/claim_key, preserves the canonical table/FTS trigger model, normalizes existing project identities transactionally, and retains stale claims through supersession instead of deletion.

Current ASP.NET Core MCP filter contract: AddCallToolFilter can wrap every CallTool request while preserving the downstream tool result. Ordinary tool failures may be returned as CallToolResult with IsError=true rather than thrown; cancellation/protocol exceptions retain their documented semantics. Talvora therefore detects thrown and returned failures, aggregates concurrent meaningful calls into one user-facing worklog card, and wraps start/progress/terminal notification side effects so observability can never alter, mask, cancel, or replace the underlying tool result.

Current Microsoft Windows/PowerShell task guidance supports manual task execution and explicit enable/disable control. Talvora uses that lifecycle for the opt-in Penpot task: disabled while idle, explicitly enabled before Start-ScheduledTask, and stopped/disabled again when the on-demand MCP is not in use.

Current .NET exception-handling guidance supports catching specific exception types at boundaries where the application can log, translate, or recover. Talvora now keeps exact exception detail in its technical logging path while Control Center and Tray translate known exception classes into plain Turkish user messages with truthful next-step guidance; unknown exceptions use a generic user-safe message instead of exposing raw exception text.

Current WPF-UI Snackbar guidance confirms presenter-owned nonmodal notification UX with explicit timeout; Talvora keeps the existing WPF-UI design language while using a tray-owned WPF progress card so full text, coalescing, hover pause and lifecycle remain under Talvora control.

Current WPF dispatcher guidance confirms UI callbacks execute through Dispatcher operations and recommends moving blocking work away from the dispatcher before marshaling results back to UI state. Talvora keeps the cross-process Mutex acquire/release wholly on one worker thread, performs bounded event-history and raw-log file reads through async worker boundaries, parallelizes independent detail health/version/event work, and uses a nonblocking gate plus selected-MCP identity check to prevent overlapping or stale live-log refreshes.
